question: For a stationary point charge in vacuum, the electric field magnitude at distance $r$ is $E \propto Q/r^2$. You first measure $E$ at distance $r$ from a charge $Q$. The source is then changed to $4Q$. State the change of distance required to keep the field magnitude equal to the original $E$.

options.A: Move to $2r$; also, if the source were $9Q$ instead, moving to $3r$ would likewise keep $E$ the same.
options.B: Move to $r/2$, because halving distance cancels the effect of increasing charge.
options.C: Keep the distance $r$ unchanged; field depends only on the medium, not on $Q$.
options.D: Move to $4r$, since the field scales as $1/r$.
